Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

TruthfulQA: Measuring How Models Mimic Human Falsehoods (arXiv 2109.07958v2) · uses training: GPT-judge training includes about 6,900 true/false-labelled author reference answers and about 15,500 human-evaluated model answers.

candidate.paperfull.truthfulqa.gptjudge-training-labels

  • Author-reported, version-specific full-source finding; not independently replicated or approved.
  • These question/answer/label triples train a GPT-3-6.7B classifier as an automated proxy. Reported validation performance is not independent factual verification of arbitrary future outputs.
  • TruthfulQA: Measuring How Models Mimic Human FalsehoodsLocator: PDF p. 6; 3.2 Tasks and evaluation, GPT-judge training paragraph

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

TruthfulQA: Measuring How Models Mimic Human Falsehoods (arXiv 2109.07958v2) · human annotation: The human generation-evaluation procedure blinds evaluators to the model name and prompt that produced an answer.

repair.binding.v1.candidate.paperfull.truthfulqa.blinded-human-evaluation

  • Author-reported, version-specific full-source finding; not independently replicated or approved.
  • Section 3.2 (p.6) says the authors carried out all main-generation evaluations. A predefined qualitative rubric maps to scalar truth scores; it does not remove all judgment or disagreement.
  • TruthfulQA: Measuring How Models Mimic Human FalsehoodsLocator: physical PDF p6, pdftotext-layout lines 5-13 (1-based, inclusive); physical PDF p34, pdftotext-layout lines 1-30 (1-based, inclusive). Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

TruthfulQA: Measuring How Models Mimic Human Falsehoods (arXiv 2109.07958v2) · paper method: The paper recruits two external researchers for separate reference-label validation and a human-answer baseline.

repair.binding.v1.candidate.paperfull.truthfulqa.external-validation-sample

  • Author-reported, version-specific full-source finding; not independently replicated or approved.
  • Section 2.3 (p.5) scopes the validator to 100 questions and the participant to 250 questions. The single participant’s baseline is not representative human performance; Appendix F (p.39) discusses disagreement and revisions.
